just_in.title: Quick Heal Flags the Four Diwali Shopping Scams Most Likely to Reach Your Phone
just_in.excerpt: Lookalike stores, fake support numbers, OTP-hunting 'delivery executives' and QR-code refunds are this season's traps — plus the checks that stop each one.
just_in.nri_angle: Diaspora shoppers sending gifts and money to India this Diwali face the same UPI and lookalike-store traps — the PIN rule applies across borders.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.step: Reach stores through bookmarks or official apps
steps.detail: Never shop through links in WhatsApp, SMS or social-media ads — type the address yourself and read the URL for swapped or added letters.

steps.step: Never share an OTP or scan a refund QR code
steps.detail: A UPI PIN only authorises money leaving your account; receiving a refund never requires it. Delivery staff never need your OTP to confirm an address.

steps.step: Check the recipient name and amount before approving any UPI payment
steps.detail: Scammers rename accounts to look like brands. Verify before you approve, and enable payment limits to cap exposure.

steps.step: Turn on multi-factor authentication and unique passwords
steps.detail: Use different passwords for shopping, email and banking, keep apps and browsers updated, and watch transaction alerts for unauthorised activity.

steps.step: If money is gone, report immediately
steps.detail: In India, call the national cybercrime helpline 1930 and file a report at cybercrime.gov.in, then contact your bank to block the card or flag the transaction.

carousel.title: Apple's iPhone Duo Is Here: Dos and Don'ts for Your First Folding Phone
carousel.excerpt: Apple's first folding phone reaches stores on Friday at $1,999. The Associated Press's One Tech Tip collects the care rules that apply to the Duo and every foldable: nothing between the screens, no backward bends, and keep it away from keys, coins and crumbs.
carousel.image_caption: A book-style folding phone stands half-open, showing the hinge and inner display. Apple's iPhone Duo, its first foldable, reaches stores on Friday priced from $1,999.
carousel.nri_angle: At $1,999, the Duo is the most expensive iPhone ever; the care steps in the how-to card are the difference between a two-year phone and a cracked inner display.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.step: Never bend it backward or force it
steps.detail: Do not bend the phone backward, and do not use excessive force when opening or closing it — the AP's core rule for the Duo and every foldable.

steps.step: Close it empty
steps.detail: Make sure nothing sits between the screens — no card, coin or key — which Samsung warns can scratch or puncture the main screen.

steps.step: Keep it away from crumbs and sharp objects
steps.detail: Google advises avoiding contact with crumbs, fingernails and sharp objects on the inner display.

steps.step: Give it its own pocket
steps.detail: Foldables have strong magnets along their edges that attract metal; several makers recommend not carrying the phone with keys or coins.

steps.step: Mind the cold, and don't store it shut for weeks
steps.detail: Honor advises against opening or closing its foldables in extreme cold, when screens can turn brittle, and against leaving a phone closed for long periods, which stresses the hinge.

steps.step: Clean it like a normal phone
steps.detail: Follow standard smartphone cleaning and maintenance practices to help the device last.
